root_cause.text: The ulpi_register_interface() error path calls kfree(ulpi) after ulpi_register() has already freed ulpi via put_device() → ulpi_dev_release() when device_register() fails, resulting in a double free.
root_cause.evidence: Commit message: "When device_register() fails, ulpi_register() calls put_device() on ulpi->dev. The device release callback ulpi_dev_release() drops the OF node reference and frees ulpi, but the current error path in ulpi_register_interface() then calls kfree(ulpi) again, causing a double free." Patch removes the kfree(ulpi) statement from the error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential double-free or incorrect memory ownership by removing the premature kfree on the error path in ulpi_register_interface.
intent_record.what: Removed the kfree(ulpi) call and the braces in the error handling block after a failed ulpi_register call, so the function now returns ERR_PTR(ret) directly without freeing the ulpi structure.
intent_record.how: On error, the ulpi structure is no longer freed; the caller is now expected to handle memory cleanup or the structure may be leaked if not freed elsewhere.

bic_trace_step.reason: The ulpi_register_interface() function at lines 238-254 allocates struct ulpi via kzalloc, then calls ulpi_register(). In ulpi_register(), if device_register() fails (line 229-230), it returns an error without indicating that the ulpi memory may have been freed by the release callback. After the error return, ulpi_register_interface() calls kfree(ulpi) (line 249), causing a double free because device_register() failure triggers put_device() → ulpi_dev_release() which already frees the same memory. The fix would be to avoid the extra kfree, for example by returning directly or setting ulpi to NULL after device_register failure.
